Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited. Our legal and procurement leads asked me to reach out for a short list of redlines and a draft SLA addendum that we can attach to the MSA/SOW. Attached is our current MSA and SOW (Acero_MSA_SOW_v3.pdf).

High level asks from AceroHealth procurement:
- Uptime: target enterprise uptime of 99.95% monthly for Dedicated capacity (we can accept slightly lower for hosted tiers).
- Latency commitments: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 500ms for inference on dedicated pools measured in steady state.
- Maintenance windows & exceptions: need clear advance-notice windows (our team prefers >=72 hours for non-emergency maintenance) and a definition for emergency maintenance.
- Service credits: clear formulas for credits, with a cap that procurement can negotiate.
- Measurement point: we need to agree whether latency/uplift is measured at Redwood edge, at customer egress, or end-to-end.

Can Redwood provide a draft SLA addendum and suggested order form language (line items and SKU definitions) for our procurement team to review? We have an internal legal review deadline of July 10 — ideally we'd have a draft by July 1 to circulate.

Also please call out any exceptions related to private/on-prem deployments or cloud provider incidents.

Thanks,
Angela Li

Angela — thank you, appreciate the clarity. Attaching an initial draft of an SLA addendum and a suggested order form spreadsheet that maps SKUs to dedicated capacity, private deployment options, and support tiers (Proposed_SLA_Addendum_draft.docx; OrderForm_LineItems.xlsx).

Quick summary of what we propose in the addendum (high level):
- SLOs: 99.90% baseline; Enterprise SLA option: 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated pools.
- Latency targets for dedicated pools: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 500ms (measured at Redwood gateway ingress in the customer region; we can discuss e2e measurement).
- Credits: tiered credit table based on monthly uptime percentage. Example: 99.0–99.89% = 10% credit; 98.0–98.99% = 25% credit; <98.0% = 50% credit. Cap at 50% of monthly fee.
- Maintenance: standard scheduled maintenance: 30 days advance notice; we can move to 72 hours for non-critical patches for Dedicated+Private if required but need to scope emergency maintenance exceptions.
- Exceptions: exclusions for force majeure, customer-caused outages, third-party cloud provider incidents.
- Measurement & reporting: Redwood will provide monthly SLO reports plus incident postmortems for severity >= P2.

Open items we want to align on: whether Acero requires latency measured end-to-end (Redwood edge -> client) or at our ingress gateway, and the specific maintenance notice window you need for Dedicated vs. Private.

If that timeline works, can we schedule a 30-minute call on July 1 to go through the draft and get legal alignment?

Thanks — attaching: Proposed_SLA_Addendum_draft.docx and OrderForm_LineItems.xlsx.

Best,

Subject: RE: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language — legal review notes

Tessa / Aditya — quick legal points after a first pass on the draft addendum:

1) Maintenance definition: we should tighten the "scheduled maintenance" definition and explicitly carve out security patches vs. feature upgrades. For security patches propose 72-hour notice; for routine upgrades we want 30-day notice.
2) Credits cap: procurement often wants uncapped credits; recommend we keep a cap at 50% of the monthly recurring charges to limit exposure. Call that out in the credit table.
3) Measurement point: do not promise end-to-end unless we can get telemetry from the customer's environment. Recommend language that primary measurement is at Redwood ingress/edge for fairness. If customer requests e2e, add a clause: "upon mutual agreement and instrumentation".
4) Third-party cloud outages: ensure we add explicit language identifying third-party outages as an exception and offer to provide vendor incident reports upon request.
5) Order form SKUs: clarify the definition of "Dedicated pool instance" (concurrency, vGPU size). Ask Product/Infra (Aditya) to define the minimum committed units so we can list them on the order form.

I can redline the doc if you want; otherwise suggest we surface these on the July 1 call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the fast turnaround and for looping legal and product. The July 1, 10:00 AM PT slot works for our team. A few quick clarifications from procurement/legal before the call:

- We can accept measurement at Redwood ingress for the initial addendum, but Acero will retain the right to request an e2e measurement clause once our engineering team has confirmed instrumentation.
- Maintenance notice: 72 hours notice for non-emergency maintenance is a hard requirement for Dedicated and Private deployments. Emergency maintenance exceptions are acceptable if clearly defined.
- Uptime: Acero prefers the 99.95% target for Dedicated. If you keep the credit cap at 50% that is likely acceptable to procurement, but please show the credit table and examples in the order form so finance can model it.
- Latency: we will circulate a short appendix with the workloads and sample p95/p99 measurements we need. Please include a row in the order form for "Latency SLAs (per workload)" so we can attach those samples.

Please send the updated addendum (v2) and the order form before the meeting so our legal/finance folks can review. Also include a DocuSign preview link if possible.

See you on Jul 1.

Thanks,
Angela
